sections.heading: Error Codes Standardization
sections.summary: Simsonraj will champion the error-code standard by pushing an initial implementation into go-ethereum, coordinating directly with Felix.
sections.body:
- The main blocking concern for error codes is `eth_simulateV1`, which uses legacy uncategorized error codes; some teams rely on it as-is.
- Simsonraj recommended leaving the `eth_simulateV1` error codes alone and tackling recategorization in a future `eth_simulate` version, since the goal of the effort is addressing end-user concerns (wallets, cross-chain compatibility). The existing categorization is "decent" enough to proceed with, modulo some cleanup.
  - Sina's earlier proposal to categorize errors as validation errors, execution errors and runtime errors was, in Simsonraj's view, not the right shape.
- No clients are currently in compliance with the proposed error-code standard.
- Chase created a PR to implement the standard, but it stalled on suggestions from Sina and Felix and the open questions those raised; the missing piece is someone pushing implementations into clients rather than more spec debate.
- Simsonraj agreed to own this: he will DM Felix, jump on a call with him separately, and get an initial version into go-ethereum. He also said he would try to talk to Sina.
  - Rationale: if go-ethereum adopts the standard, the other clients will likely follow. His framing was that some version has to go into the actual clients, or the discussion stays stuck on semantics.
  - Felix had been away but appears to be back; he is not expected to start joining RPC calls.
  - Sina no longer joins RPC Standards calls.

sections.heading: V1 Release Blockers and go-ethereum PRs
sections.summary: The V1 spec release is blocked primarily on 3-4 go-ethereum PRs that have approvals but have not been merged.
sections.body:
- [Issue #887](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/issues/887), "meta: tracking v1 release," links the outstanding work; most of what is on the agenda is covered by it.
- The biggest blockers are go-ethereum PRs (3-4 of them) that have received "looks good to me" approvals but remain unmerged. One of them is not Chase's, but it has been updated.
  - Chase pinged Marius and Felix again the morning of the call asking whether there was additional feedback or whether they could be merged. He noted both are busy with Glamsterdam work.
  - go-ethereum maintainers are more conservative about merging to main than other client teams.
- The dependency chain, in Chase's words: "We have to upgrade to Glamsterdam. In order to update to Glamsterdam, we have to fix `eth_simulateV1`. In order to fix `eth_simulateV1`, we need the go-ethereum PRs merged."
- Once those land, Chase can update the dependent PRs to target the latest go-ethereum and the majority of V1 items become unblocked for review and merge.
- Nothing on the list is blocked by disagreement or an open question — the remaining items are in conceptual agreement.

sections.heading: Blocked Check-in Items
sections.summary: Several blocked PRs were reviewed; most depend on Glamsterdam support or GoEthereum merges, with one needing spec updates.
sections.body:
Chase walked the agenda's blocked list on screen without naming most of the numbers; the items below are matched to the agenda's order.

- [#855](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/855) (`callTracer` output + `debug_traceCall`): stacked on the Amsterdam chain bump, so "kind of" blocked on the fork. The decision was taken that the log index should be **block-global**; Chase needs to write that into the spec, and PRs will then be needed to fix some clients.
- [#862](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/862) (`slotNumber`/`targetGasLimit` on `testing_buildBlockV1`): needs Glamsterdam support — same dependency.
- [#854](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/854) (`eth_createAccessList` fee affordability): depends on a go-ethereum PR; tracked in the V1 tracker.
- [#852](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/852) (EIP-8037 two-dimensional gas in tracing): more call-tracer work.
- [#856](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/856) (engine bit ordering for custody/cell bitarrays): Chase noted it looks good to him.
- [#847](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/847) (`debug_executionWitness`): waiting on an EIP — "the execution witness spec is not going anywhere for now."
- [#859](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/859) (EIP-1898 block objects in `BlockNumberOrTagOrHash`): the assigned reviewer never responded. Boma suggested CC'ing Felix; Chase raised just merging it as an option.

sections.heading: Hive Schema Validation
sections.summary: Chase's Hive PR will likely be closed in favor of Felix's more flexible WIP solution using Go scripts for schema validation.
sections.body:
- Felix has two work-in-progress PRs: one to [execution-apis](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/893) and one to [Hive](https://github.com/ethereum/hive/pull/1613), both adding support for validation scripts in test files.
- Felix's approach allows adding Go scripts into the testing files, and those scripts do the schema validation; Chase described it as a more flexible, more powerful and less messy solution to the same problem.
- Chase's own Hive PR for schema validation, [hive#1588](https://github.com/ethereum/hive/pull/1588), will likely be closed in favor of Felix's work once that is finished and merged.
- The call tracer schema work would benefit from Felix's validation scripts landing — it is not an absolute requirement, but it would let the call tracer schema be validated in a script.
- Both of Felix's PRs remain WIP, so nothing can be merged yet; no timeline was given.

sections.heading: Trace Namespace Harmonization
sections.summary: Significant cross-client differences exist in the trace namespace; next step is writing a spec, but this is post-V1 priority.
sections.body:
- crebsy brought up [issue #890](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/issues/890), "Standardizing the Parity `trace_*` APIs and their output formats," opened by banteg.
- banteg had posted findings showing significant differences in trace outputs across clients (Reth, Nethermind, Besu, and others).
- go-ethereum is the only client that does not implement the `trace` namespace; every client supports `debug`. Chase framed the question as "will go-ethereum implement the `trace` namespace?" rather than moving anyone's traces between namespaces.
  - Even among the clients that do implement `trace`, there are notable differences in response formats and semantics.
- Chase said he lacks the domain expertise to decide which client's trace output is correct; the work needs a champion who actually ingests trace data (a block indexer or explorer operator).
- crebsy's framing: if the `trace` namespace became part of the spec, clients would have to implement it and Hive tests could be written against it — and an optional-namespace carve-out might be acceptable to go-ethereum.
- Agreed approach: write the spec first (schema, inputs/outputs, mandatory vs optional fields, like any other method), then produce a table of how each client deviates and what each would have to change, then open the alignment PRs.
  - This mirrors what Chase did for the OpCode Tracer, where the per-client diff table proved far more effective at getting reviews and approvals than asking teams to read the spec line by line.
  - crebsy added that with a spec in hand the diffs could be generated automatically, and tests — or even client PRs — generated from them.
- On versioning: no Trace V2. Since there is no standard version today, standardizing the existing `trace_block` / `trace_transaction` methods in place makes more sense; a V2 would only be warranted if a consistent standard already existed.
  - The `debug` namespace is not expected to go away — too many apps rely on it.
- Chase does not expect go-ethereum to move until the other clients converge on a unified spec, at which point "5 of 6 clients agree" becomes the argument.
- This will not make the V1 release. Chase said he wants Amsterdam and V1 out the door first, then may consult banteg and start on the spec.
- crebsy suggested pinging banteg directly, since he is deeper into the trace output differences.
- Boma offered to take a look as well if it is something manageable.

sections.heading: New Contributor Availability
sections.summary: Ahmad Wilson plans to attend RPC calls more regularly and is looking for ways to contribute.
sections.body:
- Ahmad has had scheduling conflicts (US Central Time morning appointments) that have limited his attendance.
- He is working to reschedule and attend more regularly.
- He has one outstanding PR waiting on review; he cited the number as 867 but was not sure. His open PR is [#862](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/862), covered above in the blocked check-in.
